pages.x: Adolf Hitler, Germany's dictator since 1933, rearmed his country and swallowed Austria and Czechoslovakia while Britain and France, desperate to avoid a war, gave way. In August 1939 he made a pact with Stalin to split eastern Europe between them, and on 1 September his armies invaded Poland. Two days later Britain and France declared war.

In the spring of 1940 German tanks and dive-bombers overran Denmark, Norway, the Netherlands, Belgium and France in a few weeks. Over 330,000 British and French soldiers were rescued from the beaches of Dunkirk by warships and hundreds of little boats. France surrendered in June.

Britain fought on alone under its new prime minister, Winston Churchill, who offered nothing but blood, toil, tears and sweat. In the Battle of Britain that summer its fighter pilots beat off the German air force, and Hitler put off his invasion. German bombs fell on London night after night in the Blitz.

In June 1941 Hitler turned on Stalin and invaded the Soviet Union with over three million men, the largest invasion in history. By December his armies were at the gates of Moscow, and they besieged Leningrad, where some 800,000 people or more would die, most of hunger, in almost 900 days.

On 7 December 1941 Japanese planes from six aircraft carriers attacked the American fleet at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, killing some 2,400 Americans. The United States entered the war, and Hitler declared war on it too. Japan swept across Southeast Asia and the Pacific, taking Hong Kong, Malaya, Singapore, the Philippines and the Dutch East Indies.

In the summer of 1942 the Germans drove toward the Soviet oil fields and reached the city of Stalingrad on the Volga. The fighting went from street to street and house to house. In November the Red Army surrounded the German Sixth Army, and in February 1943 its last 91,000 starving men surrendered. The tide had turned.

On 6 June 1944, under General Dwight Eisenhower, more than 150,000 American, British, Canadian and other Allied soldiers landed on the beaches of Normandy, in the largest invasion ever made from the sea. By August Paris was free, and in the east the Red Army was driving the Germans back toward Berlin.

Most of the dead were civilians, killed by bombs, massacres, hunger and disease, and in the Holocaust, the Nazi murder of six million Jews. The Soviet Union lost some 27 million people, China perhaps 15 to 20 million, and Poland a sixth of all its people.
pages.of: people died, most of them civilians

pages.x: Hitler shot himself in his Berlin bunker as the Red Army closed in, and Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945. Japan fought on, until in August the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, killing some 200,000 people by the end of the year, and the Soviet Union invaded Manchuria. Japan surrendered on 15 August.

pages.x: The war left Europe in ruins and two superpowers, the United States and the Soviet Union, facing each other in a cold war. The United Nations was founded to keep the peace, Nazi leaders were tried at Nuremberg, and the European empires began to end. The atomic bomb has hung over the world ever since.
pts: Began with the invasion of Poland, 1 September 1939
Ended in August 1945, after the atomic bombs
It gave birth to the United Nations
